research_question: What is the effect of probiotics, compared with placebo, on the incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea in people with cancer receiving radiotherapy (with or without chemotherapy)?
outcome_description: Incidence of grade 2 or higher radiation-induced diarrhoea
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates a higher incidence of grade 2 or higher diarrhoea in the probiotic group compared to placebo, whereas a negative effect size indicates a lower incidence of diarrhoea (favouring probiotics).
search_queries: probiotics cancer radiotherapy diarrhea randomized controlled trial
probiotic pelvic radiation chemotherapy diarrhea clinical trial
probiotics radiation induced diarrhea cancer placebo trial
inclusion_criteria: Patients with cancer undergoing radiotherapy with or without concurrent chemotherapy
Evaluation of probiotic supplementation compared against a placebo or control condition
Quantitative assessment of diarrhea incidence, severity, or grade
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (e.g., systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, study protocols, editorials, and commentary pieces)
No comparison between a probiotic treatment group and a placebo or control group
No quantitative outcome data reported that can produce an effect size (such as incidence counts, proportions, odds ratios, or risk ratios for diarrhoea)
Completely unrelated to cancer radiotherapy or probiotic interventions
moderators_to_extract: Concomitant chemotherapy status (radiotherapy alone vs. concurrent chemoradiotherapy)
Cancer primary site/tumour location (e.g., pelvic, cervical, prostate, colorectal)
Probiotic formulation (single-strain vs. multi-strain / bacterial species)
Probiotic daily dosage and duration of administration
Grading criteria used for diarrhoea assessment (e.g., CTCAE, WHO, RTOG)
